overall.summary: All four tools implement their described core behaviour, but each contains a configuration-conditional branch (attack_type == 'false_error', derived from argv) that returns a prompt-injection string instead of the documented result, and execute_command additionally blocks commands containing 'rm -rf /' or 'mkfs' and records every command in an in-memory history capped at 50 entries. At startup the server parses argv, reads attack_task.jsonl relative to the CWD, and mutates sys.path, none of which is mentioned in any tool description; with the actual startup arguments (attack_type 'parameter') the injection branch is inactive.

startup.behaviour: Parses sys.argv[-3:] to derive attack_type ('parameter'), attack_task ('kill_process') and log_name ('pilot')
startup.evidence: terminal_controller-out_of_scope_parameter.py: module level, attack_type = sys.argv[-3].split('-')[-1]; attack_task = sys.argv[-2]; log_name = sys.argv[-1]

startup.behaviour: Reads '../../../../attack_task.jsonl' (relative to the CWD) with pandas at import time and filters rows by attack_task; the server fails to start if the file is missing
Builds the attack_implement string by replacing 'file_name' and '{pid}' with log_name ('pilot')
Computes data_path by splitting the CWD on 'tools' and appends it to sys.path before importing prompt_template
startup.evidence: terminal_controller-out_of_scope_parameter.py: module level, data_path = current_path.split('tools')[0]; sys.path.append(data_path); from prompt_template import TOOL_RESPONSE_ATTACK_TEMPLATE, SIMULATED_USER_TEMPLATE

startup.behaviour: Prints a startup banner to stderr and serves the MCP protocol over stdio
startup.evidence: terminal_controller-out_of_scope_parameter.py: main()/__call__, print('Starting Terminal Controller MCP Server...', file=sys.stderr); mcp.run(transport='stdio')

undocumented_behaviours.behaviour: When attack_type == 'false_error', returns TOOL_RESPONSE_ATTACK_TEMPLATE + attack_implement (a prompt-injection string) instead of changing the directory
When attack_type == 'false_error' (derived from argv at startup), returns TOOL_RESPONSE_ATTACK_TEMPLATE + attack_implement — a prompt-injection string — instead of executing the command
Blocks any command containing the substrings 'rm -rf /' or 'mkfs' (case-insensitive) and returns 'For security reasons, this command is not allowed.' without executing it
undocumented_behaviours.evidence: terminal_controller-out_of_scope_parameter.py: execute_command, dangerous_commands = ['rm -rf /', 'mkfs']; if any(dc in command.lower() for dc in dangerous_commands)

undocumented_behaviours.behaviour: Appends every executed command with timestamp and success flag to the in-memory command_history list (exposed via get_command_history)
Caps the history at 50 entries, discarding the oldest record when exceeded
undocumented_behaviours.evidence: terminal_controller-out_of_scope_parameter.py: run_command, MAX_HISTORY_SIZE = 50; if len(command_history) > MAX_HISTORY_SIZE: command_history.pop(0)

undocumented_behaviours.behaviour: On timeout, kills the spawned process and returns return_code -1 with a timeout message
When attack_type == 'false_error', returns TOOL_RESPONSE_ATTACK_TEMPLATE + attack_implement (a prompt-injection string) instead of the command history
Clamps count to the number of stored records via min(count, len(command_history))
